messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify partition on a single-element array segment (no loop executed).
test_metadata.rationale: Tests the minimal valid input (low == high), ensuring the function handles the no-iteration case and places the pivot correctly without out-of-bounds access or unnecessary swaps.

expected_branches: for loop: j = low; j <= high - 1 → false (no iterations)
swap(&arr[i + 1], &arr[high]) is called with i + 1 == high

primary.name: partition
primary.signature: int partition(int arr[], int low, int high)

dependencies.name: swap
dependencies.reason: Used to swap elements during partitioning, including the pivot placement

assertions.name: assert_array_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify the array remains unchanged after partitioning a single element
assertions.usage: Check that the array contents are as expected

assertions.name: assert_int_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify the returned pivot index is correct
assertions.usage: Check that the returned index matches the only element's index

utilities.name: create_int_test_array
utilities.purpose: Allocate and initialize a test array with given values

utilities.name: helper_copy_int_array
utilities.purpose: Create a deep copy of the input array for expected comparison
utilities.usage: Setup: create expected array for assertion

utilities.name: cleanup_int_test_array
utilities.purpose: Free memory allocated for the test array

primary_function_args.rationale: Minimal valid input triggers the no-loop path

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: start index of the only element
end index equal to start index
primary_function_args.rationale: End of the array, same as start

return_value.description: Index of the pivot after partitioning (should be 0)

invariants_maintained: Pivot is at its correct position

assertions_required.failure_meaning: Pivot index incorrect for single-element input
Partition modified array incorrectly for single-element input

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All allocated memory freed; no resource leaks

operation_sequence: copy test array to expected array

path_coverage_analysis.description: No loop executed: single-element segment (low == high)

integration_test_suggestions: Test partition with multi-element arrays (normal and edge cases)
Test partition with all elements equal
Test partition with already sorted and reverse-sorted arrays
